key_insight: Statistics of language exhibit a translation symmetry in token co-occurrence that forces learned embeddings to adopt simple geometric structures (e.g., months on a circle, years on a 1D manifold); the embedding geometry can be predicted from these statistical symmetries.
problem_solved: Explains why seemingly simple, low-dimensional geometric patterns repeatedly appear in large language model representations and links those patterns to corpus-level co-occurrence structure rather than idiosyncratic model artifacts.
method: Theoretical analysis: show how translation symmetry in co-occurrence statistics constrains the eigenspectrum/eigenfunctions of associated matrices and thus the geometry of learned representations.

Empirical validation: measure co-occurrence matrices from text, perform spectral decompositions, and verify predicted geometries in model embeddings (e.g., circular month layout, smooth year manifold).
Probing & diagnostics: use linear probes and reconstruction tests to demonstrate decodeability of structured features (e.g., lat/long, time) that follow from the symmetry-driven geometry.
impact: Provides a principled, data-driven explanation for common geometric motifs in LLM embeddings, improving interpretability and giving practitioners a diagnostic and predictive tool to anticipate which features will be linearly decodable from representations.
visual_elements: Circular arrangement of month tokens in embedding space (colored points on a circle) annotated with decoded month labels.
1D smooth manifold (curve) visualization for year tokens showing monotonic mapping and low-dimensional projection.
Heatmap of token co-occurrence matrix highlighting translation symmetry (repeating bands) alongside its spectral decomposition (leading eigenvectors).
Scatter plot showing linear probe decoding of geographic coordinates from embeddings with regression lines and decode-error metrics.
paper_title: Symmetry in language statistics shapes the geometry of model representations
paper_authors: Dhruva Karkada, Daniel J. Korchinski, Andres Nava, Matthieu Wyart, Yasaman Bahri
